verses.text: My son, do not forget my teaching, but let your heart keep my commandments;
for they will add length to your days, years and peace to your life.
Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
Then you will find favor and high regard in the sight of God and man.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding;
in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight.
Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil.
This will bring healing to your body and refreshment to your bones.
Honor the LORD with your wealth and with the firstfruits of all your harvest;
then your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, and do not loathe His rebuke;
for the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as does a father the son in whom he delights.
Blessed is the man who finds wisdom, the man who acquires understanding,
for she is more profitable than silver, and her gain is better than fine gold.
She is more precious than rubies; nothing you desire compares with her.
Long life is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honor.
All her ways are pleasant, and all her paths are peaceful.
She is a tree of life to those who embrace her, and those who lay hold of her are blessed.
The LORD founded the earth by wisdom and established the heavens by understanding.
By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open, and the clouds dripped with dew.
My son, do not lose sight of this: Preserve sound judgment and discernment.
They will be life to your soul and adornment to your neck.
Then you will go on your way in safety, and your foot will not stumble.
When you lie down, you will not be afraid; when you rest, your sleep will be sweet.
Do not fear sudden danger or the ruin that overtakes the wicked,
for the LORD will be your confidence and will keep your foot from the snare.
Do not withhold good from the deserving when it is within your power to act.
Do not tell your neighbor, "Come back tomorrow and I will provide"— when you already have the means.
Do not devise evil against your neighbor, for he trustfully dwells beside you.
Do not accuse a man without cause, when he has done you no harm.
Do not envy a violent man or choose any of his ways;
for the LORD detests the perverse, but He is a friend to the upright.
The curse of the LORD is on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.
He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble.
The wise will inherit honor, but fools are held up to shame.

context.author: Solomon son of David, king of Israel, according to the heading (1:1). Chapters 1-9 are a father’s speeches to his son, with Wisdom speaking for herself, and many scholars think an editor set them at the front as the book’s introduction.
context.genre: Wisdom poetry: a father’s teaching and Lady Wisdom’s speeches
context.audience: A young man (“my son”) being trained for adult life in Israel, and with him “the simple” and the wise (1:4-5)
context.mapLabel: JERUSALEM, THE ROYAL COURT OF SOLOMON
context.setting: The father promises long life and peace to the son who keeps his commands (vv.1-4). The best-known lines of the book follow: “Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding; in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight” (vv.5-6). Honor the LORD with your wealth, and accept his discipline as a father’s love (vv.9-12). Wisdom is better than silver and gold and is “a tree of life” (vv.13-18); by wisdom the LORD founded the earth (vv.19-20). The chapter ends with plain rules for neighbors: do not hold back good, do not plot harm, do not envy the violent (vv.27-35).
context.custom: “The firstfruits” (v.9) were the first and best of the harvest, brought to God at the Temple before the rest was used (Exodus 23:19; Deuteronomy 26:1-11). Storehouses and vats (v.10) held grain and wine pressed from grapes. Writing on “the tablet of your heart” (v.3) uses the picture of a scribe’s writing board, and binding commands around the neck recalls Deuteronomy 6:8.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 4 has the father pass on what his own father taught him: get wisdom, and keep to the path of the righteous.
context.timelineBible: “A tree of life” (v.18) recalls the tree in Eden (Genesis 2:9; 3:22-24), and the phrase comes back in 11:30, 13:12 and 15:4. The Lord’s discipline in vv.11-12 is quoted in Hebrews 12:5-6, and v.34 in James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5.

translation.meaning: To rely on, to feel safe in someone. It is leaning your whole weight on God.
To know. To “know Him in all your ways” is to keep God in mind in every part of life.
Training and correction, the way a father shapes a son. It can include rebuke, but its goal is growth.

gospelParallels.note: Quotes vv.11-12: the Lord disciplines the one he loves.
Quotes v.34: God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Jesus grew in favor with God and man, as v.4 promises.

otBackground.note: The tree of life in the garden.
Trust in the LORD and do good; commit your way to him.

overview.summary: Trust the LORD with all your heart, honor him with your wealth, accept his correction, and treat your neighbor well; wisdom is a tree of life.
overview.settingLine: A father teaches trust in God.

history.t: Firstfruits were brought to the Temple.
Wealth meant full barns and overflowing vats.

customs.t: The first of the harvest belonged to God.
Scribes wrote on tablets, a picture for the heart.

archaeology.t: Rock-cut winepresses with collecting vats are found all over the hill country.
Long halls with rows of pillars at Megiddo and Hazor are read by some as storehouses, by others as stables.

overview.discussion: “Lean not on your own understanding” (v.5) does not mean stop thinking. Where am I tempted to trust my own reading of a situation more than God?
overview.book: The book of Proverbs · 31 chapters. Short sayings and longer poems that teach how to live wisely in God’s world, beginning with the fear of the LORD.
overview.author: Solomon (1:1)
